item.title: Correction · Pier 70 Building 113/114/115/116 (Union Iron Works Machine Shop): The map notes no longer call…
item.description: The map notes no longer call 21st St a not-yet-built street, since DataSF lists it as an active street and the Port says its improvements were built from 2019 and accepted in 2024. They now say the 1885 and 1886 brick structures are not named 'Machine Shop' and 'Foundry' in the planning packet, and give the packet's metal-additions wording as written. They also say the old Assessor lot 4111004 was retired in 2018, replace two bare-homepage source links, and date the Port's January 2019 update to its Jan 4 memo. Source: SF Planning, Historic Preservation Commission informational packet, case 2013.1168E, 2013-11-26 (https://default.sfplanning.org/meetingarchive/planning_dept/commissions.sfplanning.org/hpcpackets/2013.1168E.pdf); National Park Service, Union Iron Works Historic District National Register nomination, 2014-04-17 (https://npgallery.nps.gov/GetAsset/99f11ae6-3834-4f99-840a-0e8a097398e6); DataSF Street Centerline (https://data.sfgov.org/dataset/Street-Centerline/3psu-pn9h); Port of San Francisco, Commission Item 11A staff report, 2026-08-07 (https://www.sfport.com/sites/default/files/2026-08/item_11a_p70_project_update_-_term_sheet_overview_-_information.pdf); DataSF Parcels (https://data.sf.gov/d/acdm-wktn); Port of San Francisco, Commission Item 12A staff report, 2019-01-04 (https://www.sfport.com/media/4465/download).

item.title: Milestone · Pier 70 Building 113/114/115/116 (Union Iron Works Machine Shop): Historic Shipyard at Pier 70… (~2023)
item.description: Historic Shipyard at Pier 70 Rehabilitation receives a Governor's Historic Preservation Award (~2023). Source: California Office of Historic Preservation, 2023.

item.title: Milestone · Pier 70 Building 113/114/115/116 (Union Iron Works Machine Shop): Port staff update to the… (Jan 4, 2019)
item.description: Port staff update to the Commission (memo dated Jan 4, 2019): six of eight buildings complete, Buildings 101 and 102 still under construction, project 100% subleased except two atrium retail spaces; whole-Historic-Core project total costs (not the cost of this building alone) rose from $81.9M at 2014 approvals to $127.0M in Table 2's '2018, Actual' column, while the memo's text gives 'an estimated $125 million at project completion in 2020'; Table 2 marks one line (Building 102's $6.7M) as a future-expenditure estimate (Jan 4, 2019). Source: Port of San Francisco, 2019-01-04.

item.description: Two small retail spaces in the Building 113 atrium still available; Orton begins activating the atrium and plaza with events (Jan 2019). Source: Port of San Francisco, 2019-01-04.

item.description: Permanent financing for the Historic Core project achieved (~Oct 2018). Source: Port of San Francisco, 2019-01-04.

item.description: Bisnow reports that Orton signed a 130,000 sq ft lease with Uber-owned Otto, a self-driving truck company, and that Historic Pier 70 is then '85% leased' (the Bisnow article's date is a report date, not the lease date) (Apr 19, 2017). Source: Bisnow (Julie Littman), 2017-04-19.

item.title: Milestone · Pier 70 Building 113/114/115/116 (Union Iron Works Machine Shop): Gusto sublease of Building… (Apr 2017)
item.description: Gusto sublease of Building 113 East (49,074 sq ft) commences, ten years, office (Apr 2017). Source: Port of San Francisco, 2019-01-04.

item.title: Under construction · Pier 70 Building 113/114/115/116 (Union Iron Works Machine Shop): Master lease approved by the… (~Jul 2015)
item.description: Master lease approved by the Board of Supervisors and fully executed, giving Orton site control; the Port's January 2019 memo says construction commenced thereafter. The National Trust (Winter 2016 issue) says the rehabilitation 'began this past September' without printing the year, which would be September 2015, while Bisnow (April 2017) says Orton began the redevelopment 'in 2014'; the sources do not agree on the start year (~Jul 2015). Source: Port of San Francisco, 2019-01-04; National Trust for Historic Preservation (Katherine Flynn), 2016; Bisnow (Julie Littman), 2017-04-19.
item.source: Port of San Francisco, 2019-01-04; National Trust for Historic Preservation (Katherine Flynn), 2016; Bisnow (Julie Littman), 2017-04-19

item.title: Milestone · Pier 70 Building 113/114/115/116 (Union Iron Works Machine Shop): Two magnitude-4.0… (~2015)
item.description: Two magnitude-4.0 earthquakes shake the Bay Area in summer 2015 while Building 113, constructed in 1885, is already described as on the verge of collapse; the National Trust's Winter 2016 issue says the building 'has since been stabilized' but gives no date for the stabilization (~2015). Source: National Trust for Historic Preservation (Katherine Flynn), 2016.
item.source: National Trust for Historic Preservation (Katherine Flynn), 2016

item.title: Existing · Pier 70 Building 113/114/115/116 (Union Iron Works Machine Shop): Eastern portion of Building… (1885)
item.description: Eastern portion of Building 113/114 (blacksmith and boiler shop) completed to civil engineer D. E. Melliss's design; western portion (machine shop) completed 1886 (NRHP, STRUCTURE magazine and the Port's Table 1 give 1885/1886; the Port memo's text and the 2013 Historic Preservation Commission packet also say 'built from 1885-1888') (1885). Source: National Park Service / California Office of Historic Preservation (nomination prepared for the Port of San Francisco by Carey & Co.), 2014-04-17; STRUCTURE magazine (Michael Gemmill, S.E.); Port of San Francisco, 2019-01-04; Port of San Francisco / SF Planning, 2013-11-26.
